final_message:
I've built the recovery plan workbook and a Word summary for the meeting. Only Scenario 3 (10-hour shift, no Grill Guard in the cell) catches up the open POs and ships the May PO on May 1. The workspace/ and attachments/ folders were empty, so the Open Purchase Orders Listing is the only data source. I checked the numbers by reading the finished workbook back.

The catch-up target is 8,080 sets of Nov–Apr POs built by Apr 12, so the April PO is in transit Apr 13. Including May, it is 9,555 sets built by Apr 30.

| Scenario | Built by Apr 12 | Built by Apr 30 | April PO ships | May PO ships | Meets requirement? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Current capacity and cells | 6,090 | 7,305 | May 10 | May 31 | **No** |
| 2. Current capacity, Grill Guard moved out | 7,425 | 9,045 | Apr 20 | May 7 (Crew Cab part on time May 1) | **No** |
| 3. 10-hour shift, Grill Guard moved out | 8,125 | 9,555 (done Apr 27) | Apr 13 | May 1 | **Yes** |

- **Scenario 1:** the Grill Guard takes one cell day a week, 14 days before Apr 30. Extended Cab is hit hardest: the past-due Nov–Jan Extended Cab POs aren't finished until Mar 13.
- **Scenario 2:** moving the Grill Guard frees 13 days, but the cell is still about 510 sets short.
- **Scenario 3:** the margin is thin. It is 45 sets (about a third of a day) at Apr 12 and 190 sets at Apr 30. Losing one production day before Apr 12, or a week's delay to the Feb 5 upgrade, pushes part of the Extended Cab April PO to Apr 16.
- **Grill Guard:** it stays on schedule in every scenario. In Scenarios 2 and 3 it runs in the running board cell one last time on Jan 26, then in the other cell from Feb 2.

**Decisions needed this week (for Scenario 3):**
- Release welding and engineering to move the Grill Guard to the other cell by Feb 1.
- Issue the 30-day notice for the staggered 10-hour day by Fri Jan 26. I set the four weeks for Feb 26 – Mar 23, which avoids both stat holidays and gives the upgrade three weeks to settle. Staff still work 8 hours each, so there's no overtime.
- Keep the Feb 5 upgrade on schedule.
- Not in the numbers, but worth doing: the cell is idle Jan 2–19, so if Grill Guard material is on hand, building the week-of-Jan-22 Grill Guards then adds about 120 sets of margin.

**Assumptions to confirm** (all listed in the deliverables):
- **Grill Guard rate:** the brief doesn't give one, so I assumed 100 units take one full shift per week. A faster rate would only improve Scenario 1.
- **Stat holidays:** Louis Riel Day (Feb 19), Good Friday (Mar 30) and Victoria Day (May 21). Easter Monday is treated as a working day.
- **May build order:** the customer gave none, so Crew Cab May is built before Extended Cab May.
- **Shipping and losses:** each PO ships the working day after it's finished, with no partial shipments and no scrap or downtime modelled, so all three plans are best case.

The workbook has a comparison sheet, the written summaries, the three daily plans in the same layout, PO completion dates by scenario, and the full assumptions. The source listing's "TOTAL Open" cells leave out May; the plan includes it.

DONE

Files are in outputs/:
- Running_Board_Recovery_Plan.xlsx
- Running_Board_Recovery_Plan_Summary.docx
